analysis: The code snippet calls `is.available()` inside the `readStream` method. The documentation for `available()` indicates it may throw `IOException` if an I/O error occurs. The calling context does not catch this exception, nor does it perform any checks (e.g., verifying that the stream is open) to prevent the IOException. Since the enclosing method `readStream` already declares `throws IOException`, any IOException from `available()` will propagate. Thus, the IOException is not avoided.
remark: The IOException can be triggered if the input stream `is` has been closed before calling `available()`, or if an underlying I/O error occurs while querying the available bytes. The code does not guard against these scenarios, so the exception may occur.
